header.body: Open Library's crowdsourced subject tags, as chips — reuses the project's existing shared Tags column (also fed by YouTube video tags and Movie's TMDB keywords), not a one-off "Subjects" header. A genre/theme split was considered and rejected: Open Library's separate 'genres' field is often empty (none for this trending result) and needs an extra per-tag lookup to resolve to a label, so the flat subject list is kept as one tag set, like Movie's keywords. External-source tag set — overlaps issue #560 (separating source tags from user tags).

cell.whenEmpty: No subjects recorded for this work.

details.title: East of Eden
details.subtitle: John Steinbeck · 1952 · 611 pages (median)
text: Steinbeck considered East of Eden to be his masterpiece. In his journal, Journal of a Novel, he notes that “this is the book I have always wanted and have worked and prayed to be able to write.” Set primarily in the Salinas Valley in the early twentieth century, the novel traces three generations of two families – the Trasks and the Hamiltons – as they grapple with the ever-present forces of good and evil.

Part allegory, part autobiography, and part epic, East of Eden was an ambitious project from the start – a gift to Steinbeck’s sons meant to teach them about identity, grief, and what it means to be human. Tinged with biblical echoes of the fall of Adam and Eve and the rivalry of Cain and Abel, this sprawling saga has captivated audiences for generations.

details.title: Brainscan
details.subtitle: Alex Wrekk · 1999 · 30 pages (median) · no cover on record
text: This issue is written in diary form and contains stories of events and situations that happened in different locations such as Utah and Portland. The author reflects upon the meaning of the past and feelings of nostalgia and belonging associated with home and homecoming.
A real, sparse Open Library record otherwise: no cover, no ratings, just three subjects. This is the row the "unknown, not zero" empty-cell rule exists for.
